question.value: Probe the ultra-bright, rare submillimetre galaxy population in the XMM-LSS field at 850 um, provide a map and source catalogue, and constrain the bright-end of the single-dish 850 um number counts.

evidence.quote: The wide area of the S2LXS XMM-LSS survey allows us to probe the ultra-bright ($S_{\rm 850\mu m}\gtrsim15\,{\rm mJy}$), yet rare submillimetre population.

The primary aims of S2LXS are to detect the most luminous and highest redshift submillimetre sources, thus providing robust constraints on the bright-end of the single-dish $850\,\mu{\rm m}$ number counts and unveiling a new distant population of SMGs.

evidence.quote: To avoid overlooking this otherwise obscure minority of the SMG population we opt for a blind source extraction approach, in keeping with S2CLS (cite: Geach2017) and S2COSMOS (cite: Simpson2019).
In keeping with recent SCUBA-2 wide-field surveys (cite: Geach2017; Simpson2019) we use the false detection rate estimates from the jackknife approach for the remainder of this work.

findings_qualitative.value: The S2LXS XMM-LSS 850 um number counts show a characteristic upturn at bright flux densities (>15 mJy) above a Schechter function fit.

evidence.quote: The S2LXS XMM-LSS observed number counts show the characteristic upturn at bright fluxes, expected to be motivated by local sources of submillimetre emission and high-redshift strongly lensed galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: There are no Galactic objects in the S2LXS XMM-LSS >5sigma catalogue, and 16 (40 per cent) of the sources have a bright, massive foreground galaxy within the SCUBA-2 beam indicative of strong lensing.

claims.hypothesis: Wide-area 850 um mapping of the 9 deg^2 XMM-LSS field can detect rare, ultra-bright (>15 mJy) submillimetre galaxies and reduce Poisson uncertainties on the bright-end of the 850 um number counts.
claims.experiment: Mapped 9 deg^2 of XMM-LSS with JCMT/SCUBA-2 for 170 hours to 1sigma ~ 4 mJy beam^-1, extracted a >5sigma source catalogue, and computed deboosted, completeness- and purity-corrected number counts using 100,000 simulated maps.
claims.result: Detected 40 sources at >5sigma (11 with deboosted fluxes >15 mJy, doubling the S2CLS sample in this regime) and measured differential and cumulative number counts at >7 mJy, finding an upturn above the Schechter fit well fit by a power law with slope -5.6 +/- 0.5.
claims.finding: The wide area of S2LXS XMM-LSS robustly measures the bright-end of the 850 um number counts above 7 mJy and reduces the Poisson errors compared to existing measurements.

evidence.quote: We present the S2LXS XMM-LSS catalogue, which comprises $40$ sources detected at ${>}5\sigma$ significance, with deboosted flux densities in the range of $7\,{\rm mJy}$ to $48\,{\rm mJy}$.
We robustly measure the bright-end of the $850\,\mu{\rm m}$ number counts at flux densities ${>}7\,{\rm mJy}$, reducing the Poisson errors compared to existing measurements.

The S2LXS XMM-LSS ${>}5\sigma$ catalogue comprises $40$ sources, of which $11$ have deboosted fluxes above $15\,{\rm mJy}$. This is twice the number of bright ($S_{\rm 850\mu m}>15\,{\rm mJy}$) extragalactic sources detected in S2CLS.

claims.hypothesis: The observed upturn in the bright-end 850 um single-dish number counts is driven by strong gravitational lensing and/or source blending within the 15 arcsec SCUBA-2 beam.
claims.experiment: Compared the corrected S2LXS XMM-LSS 850 um number counts to predictions from semi-analytic models (Galform, Shark), empirical models (SIDES, Cai-Negrello), and hydrodynamical simulations (Simba), and inspected multi-wavelength imaging for foreground lensing galaxies.
claims.result: The observed number counts are best matched by Galform, SIDES (at <30 mJy), and Cai-Negrello, which include prescriptions for strong lensing and/or source blending in a 15 arcsec beam, while 40% of the >5sigma catalogue sources have a bright foreground galaxy within the beam.
claims.finding: Both strong gravitational lensing and source blending in a 15 arcsec beam may make an important contribution to the observed over-abundance of bright single-dish 850 um selected sources.

evidence.quote: We find that the observed $850\,\mu{\rm m}$ number counts are best reproduced by model predictions that include either strong lensing or source blending from a 15 arcsec beam
The S2LXS XMM-LSS number counts are in broad agreement with the Cai-Negrello empirical model, the empirical model SIDES (at flux densities below $30\,{\rm mJy}$) and the semi-analystic model galform

why_this_data.value: XMM-LSS and E-COSMOS were selected for their wealth of legacy multi-wavelength data and accessibility to submillimetre/millimetre interferometers; wide area (>10 deg^2) at moderate depth is needed to probe rare ultra-bright (>15-20 mJy) SMGs.

evidence.quote: and so a moderate depth survey at $850\,\mu{\rm m}$ with an area ${>10}\,{\rm deg}^2$ is needed to properly probe this far-infrared luminous, and potentially high redshift population of galaxies.

These fields were selected to take advantage of the wealth of legacy multi-wavelength data available (this data is essential for identifying SMG counterparts) and for the accessibility to key submillimetre/millimetre interferometers for follow-up observations.

why_this_method.value: Blind source extraction is used instead of a prior-based approach because about 20 per cent of 850 um SMGs are undetected in sensitive near-infrared imaging.

evidence.quote: However, about $20$ per cent of SMGs that are detected at $850\,\mu{\rm m}$ are undetected in sensitive near-infrared imaging at $K\gtrsim25.7\,{\rm mag_{\rm AB}}$ (cite: Dudzevi19). To avoid overlooking this otherwise obscure minority of the SMG population we opt for a blind source extraction approach

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Processing the simultaneous 450 um SCUBA-2 data was rejected because the estimated sensitivity (1sigma ~ 50 mJy beam^-1) is insufficient to reliably detect sources.

evidence.quote: Although SCUBA-2 simultaneously collects data at both 850$\,\mu{\rm m}$ and 450$\,\mu{\rm m}$ we do not process the complementary 450$\,\mu{\rm m}$ data. At 450$\,\mu{\rm m}$ the estimated sensitivity is $1\sigma\simeq 50\,{\rm mJy\,beam}^{-1}$

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Astrometric refinement by stacking on HSC-Wide y-band data or per individual PONG scan was rejected due to inadequate signal-to-noise in the optical stack and insufficient HerMES sources per single PONG tile.

evidence.quote: In our tests (using the stacking method detailed below) with the HSC-Wide *y*-band data ($\lambda_{\rm eff} = 0.9762\,\mu{\rm m}$) we do not get an adequate signal-to-noise in the final stack for a robust measurement of the offset in $\alpha$ and $\delta$.
However, there are not a sufficient number of HerMES sources within the footprint of each PONG tile to robustly measure the astrometry offset for each observation

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Estimating the false detection rate using the inverse of the science map (with negative bowling masked) was tested as a check and gave comparable results to the adopted jackknife approach.

evidence.quote: As a check we repeat our analysis but instead of using the jackknife map to estimate the number of spurious detections, we use the inverse of the S2LXS XMM-LSS match-filtered signal-to-noise map.

how_they_decided_enough.value: The survey was scaled back from 1sigma ~ 2 mJy beam^-1 to 1sigma ~ 4 mJy beam^-1 due to bad weather on Mauna Kea, which still achieves the primary goal of uncovering the bright end; the 5sigma detection threshold was chosen to give a 90 per cent purity rate.

evidence.quote: Progress of the survey was slow due to ongoing bad weather conditions on Mauna Kea and S2LXS XMM-LSS was consequently scaled back with the revised aim to map the S2LXS XMM-LSS field to a target sensitivity of $1\sigma\simeq4\,{\rm mJy\,beam}^{-1}$.
The S2LXS XMM-LSS survey formal detection threshold of $>5\sigma$ is chosen to give a $90$ per cent purity rate.

limitations_admitted.value: Blind source extraction cannot separate multiple discrete sources blended within the coarse 15 arcsec resolution of the SCUBA-2 beam, and imposing a 15 arcsec separation limit may exclude clustered or merging sources.

evidence.quote: We caveat that a limitation of using a blind source extraction approach is that we will not separate out multiple discrete sources blended in the coarse $15$ arcsec resolution of the SCUBA-2 beam (cite: Simpson2015; Stach2018).
However, we note that if bright sources are clustered (cite: Cairns2022; Greenslade2020) or are part of merging systems, imposing this separation limit may potentially exclude some sources.

limitations_admitted.value: Number counts above 30 mJy suffer from low number statistics (only one source with observed flux >30 mJy) and large Poisson uncertainties.
